title: Learning monotone functions of bounded decision tree depth
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose deterministic decision tree depth is at most $k$, and let $\varepsilon$ be a positive learning parameter. When the low degree Fourier estimator is run on $f$ with degree parameter given by the monotone decision tree learning degree for $k$ and $\varepsilon$, the probability that its output hypothesis has relative Hamming distance strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ from $f$ is at most $1/10$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the target’s deterministic decision tree depth is at most $k$
